chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mayyah, from his father, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever speculates about Allah — how He is — is destroyed.'

key_terms.كَيْفَ هُوَ: how He is — referring to the qualitative state (kayfiyya) of God
key_terms.نَظَرَ فِي: to inquire into / to speculate about — used here in the sense of attempted rational comprehension of God's nature
key_terms.هَلَكَ: is destroyed / perishes — spiritual and eschatological ruin

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about speculating on Allah's nature or 'how He is'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a concise but emphatic prohibition against speculative inquiry into the qualitative nature (kayfiyya) of God. The teaching reflects a central tenet of Shia theological epistemology: God transcends all human conceptualization, and attempting to grasp or define His qualitative state leads one into spiritual destruction and heresy. This hadith belongs to a broader chapter in al-Kafi dedicated to forbidding anthropomorphic or speculative theological discourse about the divine essence.
